transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-18
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (CTO, LymphoHealth), Evelyn (ML Eng), Nikhil (SRE)
Resources shared: slide-deck-link: https://redwood.app/decks/lympho-aug18, bench-csv: https://redwood.app/bench/lympho-aug18.csv

00:00 Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio okay?
00:06 Marcus (LymphoHealth): Yep good here, loud and clear.
00:09 Sofia: Cool. Agenda — we'll run through the last 7 days of bench results, talk routing carveout idea and then decide the next steps. Daniel, do you want to kick with the numbers?
00:18 Daniel (Redwood SE): Sure. So we ran three seating — uh three scenarios this week. Baseline is incumbent instance (they're on Anthro-like setup), then Redwood hosted default, and then our routing-with-cache enabled run. High-level: p50 delta is about +12ms vs baseline on short prompts, p95 is closer to +85ms on long chat sessions. Throughput for sustained 4 RPS test we saw 240 tokens/sec on baseline, 270 on our tuned path when caching hits were >60%.
00:45 Evelyn (LymphoHealth): Wait, can you repeat the p95 number? You said 85ms slower?
:48 Daniel: Right, p95 85ms higher than their baseline for 1k token sequences when we weren't on the dedicated slot. But when we shifted to the dedicated lane with a quantized model variant (8-bit), p95 dropped to +12ms delta. There's a tradeoff on quality; we saw a slight bump in perplexity on few-shot tests but within acceptable thresholds.
01:12 Nikhil (LymphoHealth SRE): The quality bump — do you have the eval scores? Where were those recorded? Our concern is any degradation for clinical note summarization.
01:20 Daniel: Yes, it's in the bench CSV — column eval_qa_f1, we saw a 0.8% drop on abstractive summarization samples. Not ideal, but probably tunable via prompt ensembling and small LORA swaps.
01:33 Marcus: Hmm. For us p95 is important because of real-time triage. If Redwood can get p95 within 20ms of baseline for typical payloads, we're comfortable moving to the next stage.
01:42 Priya (Redwood): That's exactly where the carveout idea comes in. If we isolate critical traffic—say triage calls—onto dedicated slots with pre-warmed KV caches and a quantized-but-validated model, we get most of the throughput/latency upside without impacting cost for bulk non-critical traffic.
01:56 Marcus: Cost is a question. If we spin up dedicated capacity just for 10% of traffic, what's the pricing delta?
02:03 Sofia: I'll get you the delta; preliminary estimate is a 20-30% incremental committed monthly vs pure hosted but you get guaranteed p95 targets and isolation. We'll send a formal breakdown after the call.
02:12 Evelyn: On routing — can we set thresholds? Like if an incoming request matches triage pattern then route to dedicated, else fallback to hosted?
02:20 Daniel: Yes. We can match on route metadata, prompt tokens, or an explicit header from your frontend. Our routing policy can be policy-based: latency-first for triage, cost-first for batch. And we have an automatic fallback if dedicated is saturated — that keeps success rates high.
02:34 Nikhil: How does KV cache warmup work when you have pre-warmed slots? If we rotate traffic, won't cache hit-rate drop?
02:41 Daniel: Good question. The carveout plan keeps triage traffic sticky to a small pool — sticky routing uses session affinity and key-based hashing so the KV cache remains hot for those frequent prompts. For cold starts we also enable prefix caching and a short-lived warmup pool to absorb spikes. That gave us >65% cache hit rate in the tests.
02:57 Marcus: You mentioned quality delta with quantization. Have you run the specific clinical prompt set?
03:02 Daniel: We ran the 200-case clinical prompt slice — results attached in the sheet. p95 for latency on quantized dedicated slot was +9ms delta vs baseline, with avg F1 drop 0.6%.
03:15 Evelyn: 0.6% might be tolerable but we need a safety net. Can the service tag a model variant so we can always route critical queries to the full-precision variant as a fallback?
03:25 Priya: Yes — our routing supports model-variant tags in the header. If the score drops or confidence is low flagged by your post-process, the call can be retried to the full-precision model or fall back to an incumbent endpoint.
03:35 Marcus: Ok that covers routing. On throughput, you said 270 tokens/sec vs baseline 240. That's promising. Any headroom on autoscale?
03:43 Daniel: Yes, autoscale threshold and burst are configurable. For the dedicated pool we set a baseline concurrency of 32 and burst to 64 for short windows. In our stress runs that kept p95 stable. One caveat: when burst hits the host-level GPU context-switching, p95 jumps, so we recommend soft limits with queueing to preserve SLA.
04:05 Nikhil: For networking: VPC peering or private endpoint? We need to ensure no egress through public internet for PHI.
04:12 Sofia: For private deployments we offer VPC endpoints and an on-prem bundle, and for hosted we can do a private link. We'll attach our security pack (SOC2 docs, KMS integration brief).
04:21 Marcus: Do you have an audit log for every inference request? We need request lineage for compliance.
04:25 Priya: Yes — request-level audit logs are available, with optional retention windows. You can export them to your SIEM.
04:31 Marcus: Good. Back to the numbers — can we drill into the long-prompt behavior? The transcripts are noisy on long sequences.
04:37 Daniel: Sure. In the 2k token tests, baseline p95 was 420ms, Redwood default hosted was 495ms, dedicated quantized was 435ms. So dedicated gets most of the way there. The residual is mostly kernel scheduling and kv-cache miss penalties.
04:56 Evelyn: Are we seeing any mis-attribution in the transcript from the automatic capture? The CSV has a few weird tokens labeled as K/V cache but spelled kvk?k
05:03 Sofia: Yeah transcription artifacts — ignore weird casing. We'll normalize before we present to stakeholders.
05:08 Marcus: On competitor angle, how would Redwood compare to Anthropic or Vertex if we wanted a long-term migration?
05:14 Sofia: From a serving economics and observability POV, Redwood aims for predictable unit costs and per-route observability. Compared to Anthropic managed endpoints, we provide stronger batching and caching controls; vs Vertex you get a single API across private and hosted with rollout tools. But happy to do a feature matrix.
05:31 Nikhil: One more SRE detail — do you surface slow calls and stack traces for debug? We need to tie spikes to infra or model behavior.
05:39 Priya: We emit traces, per-token timing, tokenization deltas, and kernel-level counters. We can send a tracing gRPC collector or pipe to your observability.
05:48 Marcus: Alright. Let's talk decision criteria. What do you need from us to sign off to dedicated carveout pilot?
05:55 Sofia: Key things: 1) confirmation of the critical route definition (list of endpoints/patterns), 2) acceptance thresholds (p95 delta <= 20ms, quality drop <= 1%), 3) timeline and budget commitment for a 30-day dedicated pilot.
06:10 Marcus: We can compile the route list and threshold by Friday. Budget — need the exact pricing, but we can provision tentative approval.
06:18 Sofia: Great. Any blockers?
06:20 Evelyn: We want an extra run using your new batching policy (micro-batch 32) plus sticky routing for triage to confirm cache hit rate holds under realistic arrival patterns.
06:31 Daniel: We'll set that up. Could you share a 1k-sample trace of real requests (anonymized)? That helps with arrival patterns.
06:38 Marcus: Yes, we can produce an anonymized trace. Nikhil will own that.
06:42 Nikhil: I'll export and upload to the shared bench folder by EOD Thursday.
06:47 Sofia: Awesome. Quick recap of action items — Daniel export traces and attach to deck; Evelyn re-run the sample and send results; Sofia price out dedicated slots and send delta; Nikhil upload anonymized traces. We'll aim to have a decision meeting the week of 2027-08-30.
06:59 Marcus: Sounds good. Anything else on security?
07:01 Priya: We'll attach SOC2/ISO brief and a KMS integration note. One note: for on-prem we can support HSM flow, for private link we support customer-managed KMS.
07:13 Evelyn: Great. Also please add the fallback playbook for model-variant reroutes to the deck.
07:18 Daniel: Will do.
07:20 Sofia: Alright folks thanks — we'll follow up with the deck and detailed traces.
07:25 Marcus: Thanks everyone.
07:27 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mislabels, filler words present, some proper nouns slightly off (e.g., Anthropic referred to as 'Anthro' in one place).
